title: Econ Acceleration Sprint — Signal Matrix & Rollout Tracker
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: This initiative codifies a lightweight signal matrix and rollout tracker for cost optimizations across batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization. The goal is to create a repeatable experiment and rollout path that ties observable signals (latency p95, tail CPU/GPU utilization, user-facing error spike, quality delta on eval prompts) to automated guardrails and deployment gates. We will run a focused sprint of field trials on mid-volume workloads and produce a canonical decision matrix and rollout playbook for product and infra teams.
milestones: M1: Align signals and success thresholds (complete) — define 6 primary signals with owners
M2: Instrumentation + dashboard (ETA 2026-03-21) — streaming observability for signal matrix
M3: Safe experiment harness (ETA 2026-03-31) — canary + auto-rollback on signal breaches
M4: Field trials (2026-04-01 to 2026-04-10) — batching + cache + quantization permutations
M5: Decision matrix & rollout templates (due 2026-04-15) — ops & PM sign-off
success_metrics: Primary: Reduce effective per-token GPU cost by >=12% on target workloads (measured weekly)
Latency SLO: No >2% increase in 95th percentile latency for producer workloads during rollouts
Quality: Top-level eval prompt pass-rate drop <=1.5% relative to baseline
Reliability: Zero customer-facing errors attributable to rolled optimizations during canaries
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff with infra and research — agreed on initial signal set: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, CPU steal, token-rate, eval-quality delta.
2026-03-03: Research spike finished — preliminary quant profiles show 8–14% cost savings with minor quality variance on generative prompts. Booked Canopy lab for field trials.
2026-03-09: Engineering proposed adding per-route adaptive batching thresholds to avoid tail latency regressions; small API change required (ENG-19432).
2026-03-14: Dashboard prototype available: /dashboards/ops/econ-signal-matrix (internal), invited SRE and Console PMs for review 2026-03-16.
notes: Decision: Prioritize route-level targeting before global rollout to reduce blast radius.
Trade-off: Aggressive quantization profiles reduce cost but increase eval variance on multi-turn chains — will gate by eval-suite tiers.
Follow-up: Add a synthetic traffic generator for canaries to validate batching behaviour at scale (ENG spike ticket).
risks: Quality regressions in conversation-heavy flows if quant profile selection is coarse
Undetected tail latency when batching thresholds interact with bursty client patterns
Operational complexity: multiple knobs across Dedicated and Private deployments may require different rollout steps
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented dashboard showing all primary signals and automatic alerting hooks
Experiment harness that supports per-route canary with auto-rollback on defined signal breaches
Completed 3 field trials across distinct workload shapes and documented decision matrix for each
okrs_aligned: OKR-2026-Q2-1: Improve serving unit economics — contribute 12% cost reduction toward company target
OKR-2026-Q2-2: Maintain reliability SLOs while reducing cost
